commit: 79837f3 (round 1, incomplete) + ce13a5b (round 2, landed) fix(menubar): re-anchor attention bubble during drag
problem: Dragging the floating pet (Maew) while an attention bubble is displayed detaches the bubble: it stays pinned at its old anchor instead of tracking the pet during the drag.
solution: Round 1 (79837f3, INCOMPLETE) re-anchored the bubble via frameChangeHandler — but that handler fires only on mouseUp, because state persistence is deliberately deferred off the per-tick drag path for perf (phase-04). So the bubble only snapped back at drag END. Round 2 (ce13a5b, LANDED) adds a separate liveFrameChangeHandler fired from applyPanelFrame on every mouseDragged/resize tick doing a cheap in-memory bubble re-anchor; persistence stays on mouseUp. Do not collapse the two handlers back into one — the live (per-tick, no I/O) and committed (mouseUp, persists) paths have different cost budgets.
prompt_lesson: Two transferable lessons. (1) For any draggable/resizable container, enumerate every child or attached overlay (bubbles, badges, affordances, pills) and assert each tracks the same transform — coordinate-space cohesion is the UI analogue of cross-file-atomicity. (2) The round-1 miss is its own class: chrome re-anchoring must hook the LIVE per-tick move path, not a persisted-on-mouseUp handler. A perf optimization that defers state writes off the drag hot path will silently starve any overlay that piggybacks on the persist callback. When you see a deferred/debounced commit path, ask what else needed the high-frequency signal it dropped. Reachability caveat: only review-reachable when container drag-handler + overlay live in the same ticket diff; here pet (P4) and bubble (P6) shipped in different phases, so per-ticket review saw neither pair — integration-of-features bugs need a phase-level review pass.
test_reachability: Weak. Integration behavior: a real NSPanel drag emitting per-tick frame moves while an AttentionBubblePanel is live. BubbleLayout.frame is a pure function and was already correct; the regression was the missing *call* on the live drag path. FloatingPetPanelSpy (controller tests) does not exercise it. Verified by build + manual drag QA across both rounds — round 1 passed build but failed manual QA, which is exactly why ledger lines are written at verified-commit time, not on first green build.
rounds_note: Round 1 was committed+recorded prematurely (as rounds:1) before human verification and proved incomplete. Folded into one entry rather than codogotchi-02 — same bug, same gap. Methodology takeaway: when a fix does not one-shot, instrument critical paths with debug logging to find the real signal flow before guessing again (here: logging would have shown frameChangeHandler firing only on mouseUp).

problem: The Focus button in the attention bubble (1) always focused a hardcoded IDE app regardless of where the hook actually fired from, and (2) could not distinguish between VS Code forks (Cursor, Insiders, Antigravity) or reach Zed/VS Code Insiders/Antigravity embedded terminals at all. Standalone terminals (Warp, Ghostty, Terminal.app) were unreachable. Codex Desktop was misidentified as claude_code due to PascalCase event name collision.
solution: Four-layer fix: (1) CODOGOTCHI_ORIGIN=codex env var injected into Codex Desktop hook command to override PascalCase heuristic; (2) detectTerminalBundleId() in hook-binary.ts detects parent terminal from well-known env vars and writes terminal_bundle_id into source_event in state.json; (3) __CFBundleIdentifier fallback catches any IDE that directly spawns a shell without login intermediary — confirmed working for VS Code Insiders, Antigravity, Zed; (4) Focus button priority: terminal_bundle_id first → IDE-native origin map (cursor, codex) → no-op. Round 1 shipped correct architecture but missed IDE embedded terminals. Round 2 added Zed (ZED_TERM), __CFBundleIdentifier VS Code fork disambiguation, and __CFBundleIdentifier catch-all. Debug dump (CODOGOTCHI_DEBUG_TERMINAL=1 codogotchi-hook) used to validate each terminal, then stripped.
prompt_lesson: The Focus button was specified against a fixed origin→app map. No ticket asked 'what app should Focus target when origin=claude_code running in a terminal?' — the spec assumed a 1:1 mapping that doesn't exist for CLI tools. Lesson: for any user-facing action that targets an external app, the spec must enumerate the CLI-vs-IDE distinction and the embedded-terminal case explicitly. A reviewer reading the phase-06 tickets had no way to flag this because the gap was in the requirements, not the implementation.
test_reachability: None — terminal detection requires real process spawn chains. Unit-testable in isolation (detectTerminalBundleId is a pure function of env), but the end-to-end path (IDE spawns shell → hook fires → state.json written → bubble reads it → Focus tapped) is integration-only. The pure function is exported and testable; integration is verified by CODOGOTCHI_DEBUG_TERMINAL=1 spot-checks.

commit: 000375f feat(soa): append gate transition telemetry log
problem: The direct SoA gate sidecar only preserved the resident last-write-wins `gate.json` payload. Once a ticket moved through multiple gates, there was no durable record of which gates fired for that ticket or what `{ since, expires_at }` window was emitted for each one, which blocked empirical TTL tuning and post-hoc inspection.
solution: Keep `gate.json` as the renderer input, but append every emitted gate payload to `$CODOGOTCHI_HOME/gate-transitions.log` as one JSON line with the same `{ gate, since, expires_at, plan_key, ticket_id }` shape. This preserves transition order and the exact TTL window written for each emission without changing render behavior. Do not try to reconstruct history from resident `gate.json`; the append-only log is the audit trail.
prompt_lesson: When a feature intentionally uses an ephemeral last-write-wins sidecar for live behavior, ask separately whether operators also need a history lane for tuning and diagnosis. Current-state transport and observability history are different products.
test_reachability: Good. Cheap automated coverage can assert that every `writeGateEvent` call appends one line to `gate-transitions.log`, and multi-transition flows can assert ordering (`ticket_completed` before `ticket_started` in cook-mode advance). End-to-end behavior was also verified by simulating a full ticket gate sequence and by empirical confirmation that TTL still limits rendered gate lifetimes correctly.
